problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate the municipal budget across 16 different infrastructure projects to maximize the overall community benefit score.  
The profile for each project is as follows:  
* Project A: benefit score 0.169, impact factor 0.259, allocation limits [0.083, 0.882]  
* Project B: benefit score 0.104, impact factor 0.034, allocation limits [0.095, 0.564]  
* Project C: benefit score 0.121, impact factor 0.184, allocation limits [0.093, 0.453]  
* Project D: benefit score 0.099, impact factor 0.261, allocation limits [0.025, 0.654]  
* Project E: benefit score 0.136, impact factor 0.271, allocation limits [0.088, 0.594]  
* Project F: benefit score 0.027, impact factor 0.128, allocation limits [0.024, 0.525]  
* Project G: benefit score 0.049, impact factor 0.115, allocation limits [0.012, 0.869]  
* Project H: benefit score 0.045, impact factor 0.201, allocation limits [0.081, 0.490]  
* Project I: benefit score 0.067, impact factor 0.036, allocation limits [0.033, 0.554]  
* Project J: benefit score 0.165, impact factor 0.284, allocation limits [0.058, 0.710]  
* Project K: benefit score 0.139, impact factor 0.220, allocation limits [0.039, 0.878]  
* Project L: benefit score 0.052, impact factor 0.051, allocation limits [0.075, 0.828]  
* Project M: benefit score 0.173, impact factor 0.042, allocation limits [0.024, 0.862]  
* Project N: benefit score 0.193, impact factor 0.223, allocation limits [0.042, 0.518]  
* Project O: benefit score 0.107, impact factor 0.281, allocation limits [0.014, 0.729]  
* Project P: benefit score 0.024, impact factor 0.161, allocation limits [0.018, 0.793]  

Each project must receive a budget share within its specified limits, and the total allocation across all projects must equal the entire budget (sum to one).  
To ensure timely completion, the set of high-priority projects L = {A, B, C, D, E, G, H, I, J, K, L, M, O, P} must together receive at least 0.738 of the total budget.  
Additionally, the total impact factor of the portfolio must not exceed 0.246, and the overall community benefit score must be at least 0.066.  
Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total benefit score while satisfying all constraints.
